spans.text: The shrill call of a number yanks Tokarev back to reality.
She jolts, suddenly realizing she is standing in the middle of the hospital reception hall, pushing Kalina in a wheelchair.
People are milling constantly through the hospital. The lighting is harsh and white, and the air reeks of disinfectant.
The electronic display flashes the number "98". Kalina's number.
...Miss Kalina, it's our turn.
Kalina doesn't respond.
She sits quietly in the wheelchair, both hands clenched around the blood-stained Griffin uniform jacket, her gaze hollow, as if she hears nothing at all.
Tokarev lets out a soft sigh and pushes the wheelchair toward the examination room.
Inside, a middle-aged doctor is reviewing data on a screen.
She looks up at Kalina being wheeled in, then at Tokarev standing beside her with a slight frown.
You're a Doll?
...Yes.
My fr—mistress collapsed suddenly due to emotional distress. Please examine her.
The doctor steps forward, checks Kalina's pupils with a penlight, then measures her blood pressure and pulse.
Mm... She's just experiencing a mild shock. Her vital signs are stable.
Looks like extreme fatigue combined with some kind of psychological blow.
She was recently discharged, wasn't she? Still physically weak?
Yes. She was discharged only a few days ago and has been engaging in high-intensity activity ever since.
The doctor shakes her head and writes out a prescription.
It's nothing serious. She just needs proper rest and nutrition.
These are mild sedatives and nutritional supplements. Take them as directed.
Most importantly, she needs rest. No strenuous activity for at least 24 hours.
Tokarev accepts the prescription and nods.
Understood. Thank you, doctor.
The doctor hesitates, then adds quietly.
Things have been... unusual lately.
You Dolls should avoid moving around the White Zone too much.
A lot of people aren't very... friendly toward your kind.
Thank you for the warning... We'll be careful.
After leaving the hospital, Tokarev brings Kalina to one of the few surviving restaurants.
It's one of the rare places still operating in the White Zone. A handful of customers can be seen sitting inside through the glass windows.
Kalina has regained consciousness, though she still looks feeble. She glances down at the menu and suddenly clicks her tongue.
...These prices are outrageous!! This is daylight robbery!!
Seeing Kalina complain like this, Tokarev finally relaxes a little. At least her mental state is recovering.
Well, I'm here on official business anyway. The expense can be reimbursed.
In that case, give me the most expensive steak set lunch. If we're spending money, we might as well make it worthwhile.
Tokarev nods to the server.
The food arrives quickly. Despite grumbling about the prices, Kalina devours the meal with gusto.
She's clearly been starving.
Miss Kalina, are you feeling better?
Kalina swallows a bite of steak and nods.
Yeah. I was just exhausted. And... seeing that jacket hit me hard.
It brought back a lot of memories.
Her gaze drifts to the jacket resting beside her, and her expression darkens again.
But now that I've thought about it, I realize it's not something worth despairing over.
I already knew the truth... It's just an extra jacket, which doesn't prove anything.
...Yes. I agree. I also made some discoveries when investigating the site.
I believe the Commander is definitely not dead.
Inside the tank wreckage, I did find a large amount of human blood, but no human tissue, and no signs that a body was ever present.
If the Commander had truly died in the explosion, there would have been far more evidence left behind.
What's even more suspicious is that the site was barely investigated at all. Even the Doll fragments weren't recovered.
Kalina sets down her cutleries and listens to Tokarev intently.
I think the blood may indeed belong to the Commander. My guess is that the Commander was severely injured in the explosion, but did not die.
Based on the scene, I suspect someone removed the Commander from the site and deliberately staged the illusion of their death.
But... why would they do that? Who would do such a thing?
I can't be sure of the motive or the people involved.
But if we assume the Commander is alive—and injured...
Kalina's eyes widen, and she picks up Tokarev's thought immediately.
They'd need treatment! Medical supplies!
Hospitals—we need to look into hospitals!
Tokarev nods.

The Commander is currently missing. If even the authorities can't locate them, they certainly wouldn't have gone to a hospital under their own name... However, medical supplies are strictly controlled. Without hospitals, it would be extremely difficult to obtain sufficient medicine and equipment.
If we track the flow of medical supplies, there should be leads. The problem is... including the one we just visited, there are many medical facilities in the White Zone.
Finding specific information won't be easy.
Determination blazes in Kalina's eyes.
Then we investigate all of them. Hospitals, pharmacies, clinics—any place that could provide medical supplies.
If the Commander is still alive, there will be traces.
She stands up, then immediately sways as her legs threaten to buckle. Tokarev catches her in time.
Miss Kalina, you need rest.
The doctor said no strenuous activities for at least 24 hours.
Kalina shakes her head.
No. We don't have that much time.
If the Commander really is alive, they might need help right now.
We have to act quickly.
...At least finish lunch first.
We also need to formulate a proper plan.
Kalina hesitates, then sits back down and picks up her cutleries again.
This time, she eats not with frantic hunger, but with clear intention—to restore her strength in preparation for what comes next.
Tokarev... thank you.
Tokarev's electronic eyes flicker softly.
The Commander never gave up on us. We won't give up on the Commander either.
Outside the window, the sky remains overcast and gloomy.
